title: Grammar: Participle Clauses — Present, Past, and Perfect
grammarTip:
Причастные обороты (Participle clauses) заменяют более длинные придаточные:

Present Participle (-ing) = активное/одновременное действие:
"Walking home, she noticed something strange." (= while she was walking)
"Having finished the exam, he left immediately." (= after he had finished)

Past Participle (-ed/irregular) = пассивное действие:
"Written in 1984, the novel remains relevant today."
"Shocked by the news, she couldn't speak."

💡 Условие использования: подлежащее главного предложения = деятель причастного оборота!
❌ "Walking home, the rain started." (дождь не ходит домой!)
✅ "Walking home, she got caught in the rain." (она шла домой)

grammarTable.subject: Present participle (-ing)
grammarTable.verb: active, ongoing action — same time as main verb
grammarTable.example: "Burning coal releases greenhouse gases." / "Rising sea levels threaten coastal cities."

grammarTable.subject: Past participle (-ed/irregular)
grammarTable.verb: passive meaning — done to the subject
grammarTable.example: "Powered by solar energy, the factory reduced emissions." / "Damaged by pollution, the reef is dying."

grammarTable.subject: Perfect participle
grammarTable.verb: having + pp — completed before main action
grammarTable.short: having done = after doing / because of having done
grammarTable.example: "Having emitted carbon for two centuries, industrialised nations bear greatest responsibility."

grammarTable.subject: Negative participle
grammarTable.verb: not + -ing / not + pp / not having + pp
grammarTable.example: "Not knowing the scale of the problem, early industries burned fossil fuels without concern."

grammarTable.subject: Passive participle
grammarTable.example: "Being classified as a climate-critical habitat, the forest is legally protected."

grammarTable.subject: Purpose participle
grammarTable.example: "Designed to store excess solar energy, the battery system covers night-time demand."

rows.example: "Countries burning fossil fuels…" = "Countries that burn fossil fuels…"
"Talking to scientists, she realised the scale of the crisis." = "When she talked to…"
"Knowing the risks, the government acted." = "Because it knew the risks…"

rows.form: The subject of the participle MUST be the same as the main clause
rows.example: "Walking to the conference, the delegate considered her speech." ✅ NOT: "Walking to the conference, a solution was found." ❌ (Who was walking?)

rows.form: Replaces "which was/has been + pp" passive relative clauses
rows.example: "Powered by renewables, the grid is now almost carbon-free." = "The grid, which is powered by renewables, is…"

rows.form: Past participle expresses a state or condition of the subject
rows.example: "Threatened by rising seas, many island nations face existential risk."

rows.form: Common in formal, scientific, and journalistic writing
rows.example: "Produced by melting permafrost, methane accelerates warming."

rows.form: Position: beginning of sentence (most common) or mid-sentence
rows.example: "The forest, damaged by acid rain, is recovering slowly." (mid-sentence)

rows.form: The participle action happened BEFORE the main clause action
rows.example: "Having ratified the Paris Agreement, the nation committed to reaching net zero by 2050."
"Having seen the data, she could no longer claim ignorance of the risks."

rows.form: Passive perfect participle: having been + pp
rows.example: "Having been warned repeatedly, the company still refused to change its practices."

rows.form: More formal than "after doing…" or "because she had done…"
rows.example: "Having spent ten years on the issue, she understood its complexity deeply."
"Bleached by warming waters, the coral reef has lost 50% of its coverage."
"Releasing carbon stored over millions of years, fossil fuels drive climate change."
"Having reduced emissions by 40%, the country is now considered a climate leader."
"Designed to capture carbon, the new facility removes 1 million tonnes per year."
"Walking through the melting glacier, the data was striking." ❌ WHO was walking? → "Walking through the melting glacier, she found the data striking." ✅

rows.form: ❌ Wrong type: using -ing when action is completed before
rows.example: "Studying the data for ten years, she now understands…" ❌ (better: "Having studied…")
"Powering by solar energy, the factory reduced emissions." ❌ → "Powered by solar energy…" ✅
"Being damaged by pollution, the reef is dying." (correct but wordier) → "Damaged by pollution, the reef is dying." ✅

exercises.text: "___ (release) into the atmosphere, greenhouse gases trap heat from the sun."
exercises.hint: Past participle = passive: gases that are released (by burning)

exercises.text: "___ (invest) in renewable energy for a decade, the country has almost eliminated coal."
exercises.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action (they invested first, now the result)

exercises.instruction: Combine into one sentence using a participle clause.
exercises.text: "The factory was powered by solar energy. It significantly reduced its emissions." → ___ by solar energy, the factory significantly reduced its emissions.
exercises.hint: Past participle = passive: "powered by solar energy"

exercises.text: "___ the IPCC report, scientists predict more extreme weather by 2050."
exercises.hint: Present participle = active, simultaneous: "while citing / based on citing"

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct participle form.
exercises.text: "___ (warn) about the risks for decades, governments finally began to act."
exercises.hint: "Having been + pp" = passive perfect participle (warnings came first)

opts: "Burning coal, the power station produces CO2."
"Rising rapidly, sea levels threaten coastal towns."
"Walking through the forest, the data was collected."
exercises.correct: "Walking through the forest, the data was collected."
exercises.hint: Data cannot walk — subject mismatch = dangling participle

exercises.text: "___ (design) to capture carbon directly from the air, the machine removes 1,000 tonnes per year."
"___ the scale of the crisis, young people are demanding more urgent action."
exercises.hint: Present participle = because/since they understand (active, simultaneous)

exercises.text: "Because the scientists had studied the ice for twenty years, they recognised the changes immediately." → ___ the ice for twenty years, they recognised the changes immediately.
exercises.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action ("after/because of having studied")

exercises.text: "___ from permafrost as temperatures rise, methane accelerates the greenhouse effect."
exercises.hint: Past participle = passive: methane that is released FROM permafrost

exercises.text: "___ (not / reduce) its emissions, the country failed to meet its Paris Agreement targets."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses the participle clause correctly?
opts: "Built to store carbon, the forest absorbs millions of tonnes each year."
"Being built to store carbon, the forest absorbs millions of tonnes."
"Building to store carbon, the forest absorbs millions of tonnes."
"Having been built to store carbon, the forest absorbs."
exercises.correct: "Built to store carbon, the forest absorbs millions of tonnes each year."
exercises.hint: "Built to + inf" = past participle expressing purpose (designed to)

exercises.text: "___ (threaten) by rising sea levels, the Maldives has called for urgent global action."

exercises.instruction: What does this participle clause express?
exercises.text: "Having ratified the Paris Agreement, the nation committed to reaching net zero by 2050."
opts: The two actions happened at the same time
The ratification happened before the commitment
The nation is uncertain about the commitment
exercises.correct: The ratification happened before the commitment
exercises.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action before the main clause

exercises.text: "___ (produce) by burning coal, sulphur dioxide causes acid rain."
exercises.hint: Past participle = passive: "which is produced by"

exercises.instruction: Which is the most formal and economical version?
exercises.text: "Because they had cut emissions by 40%, the EU is now considered a climate leader."
opts: "Cutting emissions by 40%, the EU is now considered a climate leader."
"Having cut emissions by 40%, the EU is now considered a climate leader."
"Cut emissions by 40%, the EU is now considered a climate leader."
"Have cut emissions by 40%, the EU is now considered a climate leader."
exercises.correct: "Having cut emissions by 40%, the EU is now considered a climate leader."
exercises.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action before the main clause

questions.text: "___ by warming seas, coral reefs are dying at an alarming rate." (passive — ongoing condition)
questions.hint: Past participle = passive: "reefs which are being bleached by"

questions.text: "___ enormous quantities of carbon, the Amazon rainforest is essential to the climate system." (active — ongoing)
questions.hint: Present participle = active, ongoing: "which stores enormous quantities"

questions.text: "___ (ratify) the Paris Agreement, 195 nations committed to reducing their emissions."
questions.hint: "Having + pp" = action completed before the commitment

questions.text: "___ to prevent carbon leakage, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism imposes levies on imports."
questions.hint: "Designed to + infinitive" = past participle expressing purpose

opts: "Rising rapidly, sea levels threaten coastal cities."
"Powering the grid, solar panels reduce coal use."
"Walking through the melting glacier, the impact of warming became clear."
"Emitted by industry, CO2 accumulates in the atmosphere."
questions.correct: "Walking through the melting glacier, the impact of warming became clear."

questions.text: "Releasing carbon" and "Released by burning" have the same meaning.
questions.hint: Present participle = active; past participle = passive

questions.text: "___ (not / act) earlier on climate, governments now face much higher transition costs."
"___ from melting glaciers, fresh water floods coastal areas and disrupts ecosystems." (released from)
questions.hint: Past participle = passive: "water which is released from"

questions.text: "___ (invest) heavily in offshore wind, the country has become one of the world's leading clean energy producers."
questions.hint: "Having + pp" = prior investment led to current status

questions.text: "___ the data carefully, scientists predict more extreme weather events in the coming decades." (while analysing)
"___ (build) to withstand rising sea levels, the new seawall protects over 50,000 homes."
questions.hint: "Built to + infinitive" = past participle of purpose

questions.text: What does the perfect participle express in: "Having signed the agreement, the government faced pressure to deliver."
opts: The signing and pressure happen at the same time
The signing happened before and caused the pressure
The government is uncertain about signing
The government is planning to sign
questions.correct: The signing happened before and caused the pressure
questions.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action that explains or causes the main clause
